evidence: src/presentation/api/WorkshopController.ts openOrder: `if (input.estimatedHours <= 0 || input.estimatedHours > 40) { throw new FleetError('Estimates must be between 0 and 40 hours', 400); }` enforces a business limit on work-order estimates, which belongs in the domain layer.
The other methods (logHours, closeOrder, reading) only hand off to business services and format results, which fits the presentation role.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of WorkshopController does normal presentation work. It takes input DTOs, hands the work to the business services MaintenanceService and MileageService, and formats responses with workOrderJson. openOrder is the exception: it checks that estimated hours are greater than 0 and no more than 40, and throws a FleetError if they are not. A 40-hour maximum on a work-order estimate is a business policy, not a check on request shape or syntax. That makes it a domain responsibility (the business layer), and it should live in MaintenanceService.open or the work-order model. In the controller, the rule is skipped by any other caller of MaintenanceService.open.
